stem: Which factor most increases the likelihood that a paediatric fracture will remodel successfully?

options.text: The fracture is in the diaphysis
The deformity is at right angles to the adjacent joint's plane of motion
There is more than two years of skeletal growth remaining
The child is near skeletal maturity

explanation: More than two years of skeletal growth remaining is the strongest factor favouring fracture remodelling in a child, because ongoing growth allows gradual correction of the initial deformity.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because diaphyseal fractures remodel less well than fractures nearer the metaphysis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because deformities that are not aligned with the plane of joint motion remodel poorly.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because more than two years of remaining skeletal growth gives the bone enough time to remodel and correct deformity.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because rotational deformity is poorly corrected by normal remodelling.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because remodelling potential is reduced as a child approaches skeletal maturity.

source.hint: Consider the relationship between the time left for growth and the bone's capacity to reshape itself.
